newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FALDO LEADS GRAND SLAM OF GOLF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO LEADS GRAND SLAM OF GOLF.

text.p: Masters champion Nick Faldo birdied three of the four par-three holes and sloshed his way to a five-under-par 67 and a one-stroke lead after the first 18 holes Wednesday morning at the MasterCard PGA Grand Slam of Golf over the soggy Poipu Bay Resort golf course.
"The course was pretty wet in spots, but all considered, it was in good shape," said British Open winner Tom Lehman, whose 68 left him close on Faldo's trail.
U.S. Open champion Steve Jones was another two shots back after a two-under 70, while PGA winner Mark Brooks was in the back of the pack after a two-over 74 on the 6,959-yard course.
The 36-hole tournament, which features an elite field of this year's four major championship winners, was delayed a day when heavy rains pounded Hawaii's Garden Island on Tuesday.
While the rain stayed away Wednesday, the course remained very wet and players were allowed to lift, clean and place their golf balls in the fairway.
Nine more holes were scheduled to be played Wednesday afternoon with the final nine to be completed Thursday morning.

Faldo, owner of three Masters and three British Open titles, took his lead early in the round and never looked back. The Englishman birdied holes 2, 3, 8 and 9 to make the turn in 32 and added birdies on 11 and 12 to go six under.
At that point he led Lehman and Jones each by four. But Faldo's bogeys at 13 and 16 enabled Lehman, who birdied 13 and 14, to close within one. Both birdied 17 and parred 18.
"I was on a roll there," Faldo said of his six birdies over the first 12 holes. "Then I just lost momentum coming in. Starting at 13, nothing much happened.
"Right now my feet are soaked and I can't wait to get out of these shoes," Faldo said.

Faldo said his play on the par threes was the key to his round. He birdied the 209-yard third hole from nine feet, added another at the 193-yard 11th from 15 feet, and knocked in a five-footer at the 199-yard 17th.
Lehman, who this season became only the 10th player ever to win both the Vardon Trophy for low scoring average and the PGA of America Player of the Year, had a six-birdie, two-bogey round.

"I made some good putts, but I had a lot of putts that burned the lip and just didn't go in," said Lehman, who also won the PGA Tour Championship this season and finished number one on the money list.
Jones could relate. Time after time his putts took dead aim at the hole only to slip past.
"I was just a little confused on the greens," said Jones, who had two-bogeys and four birdies, but none over the last 11 holes. "I just couldn't get the right read on them."
Brooks was the first-hole leader after a birdie, but he shot himself in the foot with a bogey at the par-four fifth hole and a double-bogey at the par-three, 157-yard seventh.

At number 5, Brooks's tee shot found a fairway bunker on the right and he left his next shot in the sand. Two holes later, he four-putted from 35 feet, missing a five-footer for par and a three-footer coming back.
"I just played bad. It's that simple," Brooks said. "Hopefully I can come back and play decently the rest of the way."
